provenance:
HELD-OUT, FROZEN AT AUTHORING 2026-08-26 (D6) — labels written and committed BEFORE the first run, per evals/heldout/README.md. Citigroup Inc. FY2025 10-K, sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831001/000083100126000011/c-20251231.htm, accession 0000831001-26-000011, filed 2026-02-20, period end 2025-12-31, 16,150,764 bytes, iXBRL — the largest file in either set. WHY THIS FILING: it is the second of the two filings that failed live at the 2026-08-24 demo (docs/evals/audits/2026-08-25-demo-intel-citi-postmortem.md), Citigroup appears in NO fixture, golden, adversarial or held-out case anywhere in this repo, and it is the money-center-bank class the postmortem §4 ranks first among known-difficult filers. It is also the most recent Citigroup 10-K on EDGAR — the only 10-K in the CIK 831001 recent-submissions window — so it is exactly what a user tries today.

VERIFICATION. Independent tag-strip regex scan (tags -> single space, entities unescaped, whitespace collapsed; imports NOTHING from src/) plus raw-byte greps for every character-level claim. The extractor has never been invoked on this file. Scan size 1,507,550 chars from 16,150,764 raw bytes; the first ~348,000 scan chars are the iXBRL hidden-fact block, and the cover begins after it.

STRUCTURAL FINDING (a hypothesis at paragraph granularity until a run tests it) AND ITS CHARACTER-LEVEL BACKING (read from raw bytes, so claimed): this filing contains ZERO occurrences of the string 'Item <digit>' naming a 10-K item code. Raw-byte counts in the 16,150,764-byte file: 'Item 1.' 0x, 'Item 1A' 0x, 'Item 7' 0x, 'Item 8' 0x, 'ITEM ' (uppercase) 0x. The regex `(?i)items?\s*[0-9]` returns 3 hits in the whole file, and none is a 10-K heading: the cover's combined pointer 'Items 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 of Part III' (raw offset 1,828,047) and two Regulation S-K citations, 'Item 402(v)' at raw offset 1,859,455 and 'Item 408' at raw offset 15,875,549. (Corrected under PR #52 R4, which is now pinned by evals/adversarial/heldout-provenance-claims.json: this sentence originally said 'exactly four hits' without naming a regex, and counted 'Reconciling Items' as the fourth — a phrase containing no digit, which no item-plus-digit regex can match. The loosest regex that would return more, `(?i)item[^<]{0,4}[0-9]`, returns 8 hits, the five extras being 'Items)”' where the digits come from the entity. The load-bearing claim is unaffected and was re-derived: no `Item <digit>` string in this file names a 10-K item.) The document maps itself to the SEC form via a 'FORM 10-K CROSS-REFERENCE INDEX' (scan offset 352,469, raw-byte count 1x) whose rows are BARE codes with no 'Item' prefix — '1. Business 4-36, 121-127, 129, 160-164, 299-300', '1A. Risk Factors 49-62', '1B. Unresolved Staff Comments Not Applicable', and so on. That is the axp-2008 bare-code shape (evals/fixtures/axp-2008), on a filing that carries it for EVERY item rather than for four.

The index lists 22 codes: 1, 1A, 1B, 1C, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 7A, 8, 9, 9A, 9B, 9C, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. Item 16 (Form 10-K Summary, optional) is absent from it. Items 10-14 are answered by the cover sentence plus five asterisk footnotes pointing into the 2026 proxy statement. Not Applicable per the index: 1B, 2, 4, 9, 9C.

COVER DATE — AND A TRAP AVOIDED. The scan renders the cover as 'For the fiscal year ended December 31 , 2025', i.e. with the pgr-2023 'floating comma'. THAT IS A SCAN ARTIFACT AND IS NOT CLAIMED. The raw bytes read 'For the fiscal year ended <ix:nonNumeric ...>December 31</ix:nonNumeric>, 2025' — the space is a tag boundary the scan turns into a character, exactly the instrument failure the README's authoring-discipline section records for pgr-2023. Raw-byte counts: 'December 31, 2025' 159x, 'December 31 , 2025' 0x. Period end is 2025-12-31 and there is no floating comma.

ANCHORS, raw-byte counts in the whole file: 'As a large, global financial institution, Citi faces particularly complex' 1x — the second sentence of the RISK FACTORS section, scan offset ~503,000; 'DISCLOSURE CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES' 2x (the contents page and the body heading at scan 833,976, which is Item 9A territory, so it is the bleed tripwire for item 1A).

LENGTH FLOORS, measured from the scan with wide margins so they cannot encode the scan's known disagreement with the normalizer. RISK FACTORS is a single contiguous section the index maps 1:1 to Item 1A: scan 502,951 to 587,719 ('SUSTAINABILITY'), ~84,800 chars, floored at 20,000. CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS through the notes runs scan ~855,700 to ~1,435,500 ('FINANCIAL DATA SUPPLEMENT'), ~580,000 chars, and the index maps Item 8 to exactly that page range (134-298), floored at 100,000. Items 1 and 7 are floored at a deliberately LOOSE 2,000 because the index maps each to several DISCONTIGUOUS page ranges, so no single span is demonstrably the right answer; 2,000 is the postmortem §5 figure for the cheapest instrument that catches a stub collapse.

WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ASSERT. (a) A status for item 16 — the index omits it entirely, so `omitted` is the natural reading, but that is an enum judgment about the contract rather than a statement the document makes, and the csco-2016 precedent declined exactly this shape of negative after H1 caught it being wrong on xom-2021. It rides in expected_set_complete, which accepts any valid status. (b) Statuses for 1B, 2, 4, 9, 9C ('Not Applicable' per the index) for the same reason. (c) `incorporated_by_reference` on 10-14: the pointer is on the COVER and in index footnotes, not in any item body — how the pipeline ought to resolve that is a design question D9/D11 own, not ground truth. (d) `deterministic` — omitted on purpose, and this is the ONLY check csco-2016's shape carries that this case drops: at 16.1 MB it would double the run cost of the single most expensive case in the repo, and determinism is already pinned by every other case in the suite. (e) Any max_chars, any confidence value, anything about the iXBRL hidden-fact block. (f) **`doc_status`** — deliberately not asserted, and this declination was undeclared until PR #52 R6 caught it. Three of the five incumbent held-out cases do assert it. The reason it is dropped here is the same as on intc-2025: `doc_status` is the signal the postmortem §2 says lied at the demo, so the honest verdict for a document in which nothing resolves is a question D8/D9/D11 must ANSWER, not one this exam may presuppose. The frozen prediction below records what I expect it to be, which is the right register for a guess about a policy under revision.

PREDICTION, FROZEN BEFORE THE FIRST RUN so it cannot be retrofitted, and NOT asserted as a check. THIS CASE IS EXPECTED TO FAIL; that is the recorded outcome of D6, not a defect to fix here (the fixes are D8/D9/D11). Because the raw bytes carry no 'Item N' string at all, I expect NO heading candidates to be generated anywhere in the document, hence all 23 era items reported `missing` with null offsets at BASE_MISSING 0.40, `expected_items_mostly_missing` firing, and doc_status `ambiguous`. That is the LOW-confidence face of the D8 sensor problem (postmortem §8: unmatched headings land 0.40, headings matched to the wrong instances land 0.95) — the opposite face from intc-2025, which is why the two filings together are worth more than either alone. NOTE THE TENSION AND THAT I AM NOT RESOLVING IT: the demo reported per-item `conf 0.95` on Citigroup, which my structural reading does not predict; either the demo ran a different Citigroup document, or a heading path I cannot see from a tag-strip scan produces candidates anyway. The run settles it; I am recording the disagreement rather than assuming my scan wins.

BURN RULE: the moment this case's outcome influences implementation — a fix, a threshold, a declined fix documented with its outcome in hand, or a new case authored from it — it moves to evals/adversarial/ and is replaced. D11 must pass this filing WITHOUT ever having trained on it; the dev-side proxies for the pointer class are cvx-2015 and jpm-2024, both already in the dev set. 

BURN RECORD, 2026-08-28. Ordering, stated plainly rather than implied: the pre-fix numbers above were measured in-session BEFORE the Citi-driven extension of `src/sec10k/xref.py`, but this was a directed sweep of a curated hard-filing list, not a milestone held-out run, so no report was committed between the measurement and the fix. What IS committed is the post-fix held-out report and this record. The held-out set is now 4 cases (cost-2022, csco-2016, mrk-1995, pgr-2023); two replacement filings are owed at the next expansion, per the budget rule in evals/heldout/README.md.

triage.note: BURNED HELD-OUT CASE, moved here 2026-08-28 under evals/heldout/README.md's burn rule, and the burn is INFLUENCE: this filing's outcome changed the implementation. PRE-FIX, MEASURED BEFORE ANY CITI-DRIVEN CHANGE: doc_status `ambiguous`, meta.coverage 0.0000, all 23 items `missing`, zero item headings found in 1,163,303 characters. The cause is one line of typography. Citi carries a `FORM 10-K CROSS-REFERENCE INDEX` — the same instrument Intel FY2024 uses — but at the FRONT of the document, and it writes its rows WITHOUT the word Item (`1. Business 4–36, 121–127, ...`) and without the word Page. `find_candidates` matches `Item N`, so it found nothing at all: not a bad span, no span. ADR-042 was authored from Intel and then extended for this shape (front-of-document index, bare `N.` rows, en-dash ranges, a page column instead of a `Pages` keyword). That extension is the influence, and it is why this case is no longer held out. POST-FIX: 11 items take the index's own rows as their spans (`method: cross_reference_index`; rows partition the index region, so they are ordered and disjoint, which is what INV-S1 asks) and their page references resolve to 1.9 MB of real content under `evidence.cross_reference` — item 1 to 164,021 chars opening 'OVERVIEW / Citigroup’s history dates back to the founding of the City...', item 7 to 296,268 opening 'MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS...', item 8 to 582,266 opening 'CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS'. The FROZEN 1A anchor authored 2026-08-26 — 'As a large, global financial institution, Citi faces particularly complex' — is inside the resolved 1A region, which is the strongest evidence here that the resolution is right rather than merely large: that string was written down before the resolver existed. WHY THE FOUR `min_chars` CHECKS STAY AND STAY RED — they are kept verbatim as recorded debt, exactly as `cvx-2015-internal-pointer.json` keeps its two. They assert the CONTENT is inside `start`/`end`, and ADR-042 §a rules that impossible for this shape rather than merely unbuilt: Citi's item 7A resolves to pages 64–120, 165–169, 190–228 and 235–278, threaded through item 8's 134–298, so the ranges overlap and nest and no assignment of them to spans satisfies INV-S1. Their red now means 'the contract forbids this', not 'this is broken'. The `cross_reference` checks added beside them are the achievable statement of the same fact. DOC_STATUS STAYS `ambiguous` AND THE COLLAPSE WARNINGS STAY FIRED. The spans really are index rows, 0.06% of the document; resolution adds an answer and does not withdraw the admission. The `not_contains` check pins that no resolved region reaches back into the index itself.
